recentItems.title: Sydney residents seek clarity as gangland war becomes political issue | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
A soundbite from a veteran detective has ignited a political war of words over gangland violence in Sydney.
The number of organised crime murders in the state has remained relatively consistent with previous years.
But a spate of fatal shootings in Western Sydney has residents questioning whether they're willing to accept gangland violence as "part and parcel" to life in a big city.

recentItems.title: Oil surge leads to ASX and bond sell-off, higher risk of RBA rate hike | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Around $90 billion has been wiped off the value of Australian shares this week. The ASX 200 index has dropped 6 per cent since hitting a record high in early August. 

Iran-backed Houthis have seized control of a key port in Yemen, posing a further threat to Red Sea traffic. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed as fighting between the US and Iran intensifies. The increased the risk of oil shortages and inflation staying higher for longer led to government bonds being sold off across Australia, the US, UK, Japan, Germany and other countries — pushing up the borrowing costs for those nations. 

Markets are now betting the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) could lift interest rates as much as six times in the current rate-hiking cycle. Presented by David Chau.

*EDITOR'S NOTE (11/09/26):* This video was re-uploaded to correct numerical errors in the graphs titled 'higher borrowing costs for Australia' and 'global bond sell-off'.

recentItems.title: Nepal demands compensation and climate justice after deadly floods | Asia News Week | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Nepali officials will seek billions of dollars from wealthier countries and global agencies for financial help, arguing they should contribute to the $5 billion needed for initial rebuilding as the disaster shows how climate change has hit poor countries that did little to cause it. 

The country is still reeling from the collapse of a Himalayan glacier in late August that's killed more than 1300 people, with thousands more still missing.

Senior news editor at Nepal Television Shivanee Thapa Basnyat tells Asia News Week's Yvonne Yong that people are questioning how prepared the state was for a disaster of this scale, and whether international expertise could have been brought in faster.

recentItems.title: RBA must hike now says Van Eck, as bond yields rise and oil prices surge | The Business | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Investors bailed out of the Australian share market this week as nerves grow the RBA will raise interest rates sooner rather than later. Russel Chesler, head of investments and capital markets at Van Eck told Alicia Barry, "we had an inflation problem before the Iran war." 

He says the Reserve Bank now needs to take quick action to bring inflation down. "The RBA needs to work really hard to get back in the 2 to 3 per cent range, they've said they can do it by the end of 2027. So I'm saying there's going to be an increase now.. (but) is that going to be enough, are we going to need another rate increase?" He said. 

Financial market are pricing in an 87 per cent chance of an increase in interest rates to 4.6 per cent on September 29.

A hike by the end of the year is fully priced in. 

The ASX 200 ended the week off 2.9 per cent to 8,741 after two days of heavy selling at the end of the week.

Investors are worried about the inflationary impact of rising oil prices. Brent crude topped $US108 a barrel on Friday.

Those concerns are showing up in the bond market. On Friday, the US 10-year Treasury yield neared 5 per cent, a key psychological threshold for global markets because it is a key benchmark for borrowing costs across the US economy, influencing everything from mortgages to corporate debt.

Australian government bond yields followed, the 10-year yield rose 13 basis points to 5.38 per cent.
